implementation_result.premise_verified_not_assumed: The MT premise (TEST wrong, PRODUCT correct) was re-derived from source rather than accepted from the MT-029 agent. invalidate_search_inputs() at find_in_files.rs:2117 deliberately omits self.results and self.result_set_key from what it clears, with the in-code rationale at 2120-2124. run_preview_replace() at 2709 compares result_set_key against current_search_key() and, on mismatch, emits "Search results are stale; run Search again before previewing replacements." Clearing the results would make that comparison unreachable because Preview would be disabled. The product is contract-correct; the assertion was drift.
implementation_result.exact_behaviour_derived_before_editing: with_visible_indices() at 2046 compiles NO regex when the query is non-empty but no match-option is active (case_sensitive/whole_word/is_regex all false, which is exactly the restored bookmark), so indices = every retained hit. visible_result_count() is therefore 1, NOT 0. Both assertions on lines 5387-5388 were wrong, not just the first. Derived from source before writing the replacement rather than guessing from the panic.
implementation_result.fix: Test-only. Replaced the two contract-violating assertions with the real contract: results RETAINED (len 1), result_set_key RETAINED and now reading STALE against the restored bookmark params (assert_ne against current_search_key), visible cache invalidated and RECOMPUTED to 1, generation advanced, pending reads and search_cell drained. Each assertion carries a message naming MT-029 AC-7 so the next reader does not re-break it.
implementation_result.hardening_added_beyond_the_minimum: AC-114-2 satisfied through the REAL path rather than a hand-built stale state: after restore_bookmark the test now constructs a RichDocClient and calls run_preview_replace, asserting the stale warning FIRES and preview_plans stays empty. The pre-existing preview_stale_result_guard test only ever proved the guard against a manually-assigned result_set_key; this proves the retention performed by restore_bookmark is what keeps AC-7 reachable. If a future change clears results in invalidate_search_inputs, this assertion now goes red with the reason attached.

scope.summary: Correct the stale assertion in restore_bookmark_centrally_invalidates_results_cache_and_pending_reads so it matches the AC-7 stale-result-guard contract that MT-029 deliberately implemented.

the_defect_is_in_the_test_not_the_produc.why_the_product_is_correct: invalidate_search_inputs() deliberately RETAINS the result set, with an in-code rationale: "Keep the last completed result set and its producer key long enough for the mounted Preview action to report the contract explicit stale-result warning. Clearing either here made the button disabled, so the UI could never exercise the stale guard."
the_defect_is_in_the_test_not_the_produc.contract_that_requires_retention: MT-029 AC-7: "Stale-result guard: if query changes after search and before preview, Preview Replace shows Search results are stale; run Search again." Clearing results/result_set_key makes Preview DISABLED, so the guard becomes unreachable and AC-7 cannot hold. Fixing the product to satisfy this assertion would therefore silently BREAK a validated acceptance criterion.
the_defect_is_in_the_test_not_the_produc.conclusion: The implementation is contract-correct. The assertion is stale drift left behind by MT-029 own stale-guard remediation. The fix is a contract-aligned test-expectation correction, not a product change.

AC-114-3: the test passes, and no product behaviour in find_in_files.rs is altered to achieve it. Any product change is an automatic rejection of this MT premise and must be escalated instead.
